thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE to oncall-sre (jay) — GPU pool congestion + autoscaler hit. Queue > 4.8k, 95th latency > 3.5s, error rate for /v1/generate up to 7%. Investigate driver/runtime errors (Xid/OOM) and autoscale behavior. Links: https://dash.internal/redwood/gpu-pools/tx-3

jay: on it. I can see autoscaler metrics: target replicas 120, max_replicas=120, currently at 120. Backlog has been increasing for ~18m.

alex: adding logs — runtime on node gpu-w-12 shows repeated CUDA/Xid events and driver process restart loops. Sample log: 
```
2026-03-15T21:18:05Z driver: cuda: Xid 701 — GPU OOM at kernel launch
2026-03-15T21:18:06Z runtime: process restart (exit code 137)
2026-03-15T21:18:07Z kubelet: eviction: pods evicted due to memory pressure
```

maria: nodes with highest evictions: gpu-w-12, gpu-w-18, gpu-w-20. Memory used on those nodes (nvidia-smi snapshot): `used 38.6 GiB / 40.0 GiB` — KV cache thrash likely.

jay: hypothesis — driver runtime encountering OOM on long KV cache + large batch combos, causing Xid errors -> node-level instability -> effective capacity lower than reported -> autoscaler keeps hitting max but cannot recover capacity.

lina: customer-impact quick note: some persistent customers (prod-critical) seeing ~10-20% increased timeout responses and elevated token-per-second billing spikes because of retries. CS asked for ETA.

alex: immediate mitigations I recommend (quick, reversible):
- route traffic for heavy long-context workloads to quantized-small model variant (model-q4_0) to reduce per-request GPU memory
- temporarily disable large-batch multiplexer on the affected pool (reduce max_batch_size to 1) to avoid memory blowouts
- increase autoscaler cap for the pool to +30 replicas if spare quota available (manual scale up)

jay: agree. I'm going to:
1) patch route rules to send requests with header `x-workload=long-context` to `model-q4_0` via the routing layer.
2) submit a quick scaling action: `infra scale-gpu-pool tx-3 --replicas 150 --reason "incident 1719004321 manual bump"`
3) cordon the most flapping nodes for investigation: `kubectl cordon gpu-w-12` then drain with `kubectl drain gpu-w-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.

maria: caution — draining will momentarily bump backlog as pods restart on other nodes. We should do route cutover first. Also we have 2 reserved dedicated pools for enterprise customers — we can divert enterprise traffic there to reduce impact.

product: please prepare a short customer note: impacted endpoints, mitigation in progress, ETA rough. Lina can you draft?

lina: drafting now. Short version: "We're aware of increased latencies/errors for text generation. We've identified GPU runtime instability causing capacity reduction and are routing heavy workloads to a lower-memory model and adding capacity. We'll update in 30m."

alex: ops commands I'm running now (posting for audit):
```
# snapshot memory per process
ssh gpu-w-12 sudo nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv
# restart driver runtime on node after cordon
ssh gpu-w-12 sudo systemctl restart redwood-driver || journalctl -u redwood-driver -n 200
```

jay: executed route patch and reduce-batching change. Patch id: rp-20260315-87. Autoscaler manual scale started. Current replicas: 120 -> scaling to 150 (pending cloud alloc).

incident-bot: Autoscaler request queued (request id asg-9876). Cloud quota check: spare GPUs available in us-west-2 region: 40.

maria: manual scale completed for pool tx-3 -> replicas=150. Observability: backlog decreased from 4800 -> 2200 in ~6m since routing change. Latency p95 improved 3.5s -> 2.1s. Error rate down to 3.2%.

alex: however, two nodes (gpu-w-12, gpu-w-18) still showing repeated Xid 701 / process restarts after we drained. I'm taking them out of rotation and tagging for kernel update and driver stack rollback.

jay: I'm going to enable temporary fallback policy: any request that would route to tx-3 getting throttled >1500 queue position will be routed to Hosted fallback pool (lower-cost but lower throughput) to avoid customer-visible errors. Implemented via routing rule rf-317.

product: good. Lina, send initial customer message now. Also toggle support escalation to Priority P2+.

lina: sent message to affected accounts (enterprise list). CS confirmation pending.

pagerbot: :pager: oncall escalation — handover to alex in 40 minutes. Current assignee jay -> alex.

jay: summary for handoff to alex:
- root cause (working hypothesis): driver/runtime OOMs (CUDA/Xid 701) under certain KV-cache + large-batch patterns -> node flaps -> effective capacity reduction -> autoscaler hit max -> queue growth and throttling.
- mitigations applied: routing long-context to quantized variant, reduced batching, manual scale to 150 replicas, cordoned/flushed two badly-flapping nodes, fallback routing rf-317.
- remaining work: kernel/driver rollback or patch on flapping nodes, postmortem collection (logs + core dumps), verify autoscaler backoff heuristics to avoid hitting max without draining, confirm customer KPIs back to baseline.
- important links: metrics: https://dash.internal/redwood/gpu-pools/tx-3, logs: https://logs.internal/tx-3?range=30m, runbook: https://runbooks.internal/gpu-instability

alex: taking over. I'll continue live mitigation: coordinate node driver rollbacks and schedule a short maintenance for those two nodes. Will also open an infra ticket to review quantization fallback as permanent guardrail.

jay: thanks — handoff complete. I'll remain available for questions. :white_check_mark:
